segments.title: Chương 95: 0095【Nữ Hiệp Ngao】
segments.content:
Chapter 98 0095 Heroine Ao (Bonus chapter for Alliance Leader 54 Gou)

"Are you free tonight?"

"Yes."

"Let's splurge, AA. Meet at the South Gate at 7:30 PM."

This was a text message exchange with his counselor, Long Xiang.

As for "splurging," it meant not eating at the cafeteria but going out for a meal off-campus.

These days, a Peking University student's monthly living expense was about three to five hundred yuan. Anyone with over 500 yuan was considered rich, and those with under 300 yuan were quite frugal.

For students, going out for a feast at the South Gate was already considered a "splurge."

The Yuanpei Program's 140-plus students were divided into 14 "ten-person groups."

Chen Guilang's group had 11 people: 6 boys and 5 girls. They had never all gotten together privately since classes started. Their group counselor, Senior Long Xiang, probably wanted everyone to gather.

Today was September 24th, the Friday of the second week of classes. The National Day holiday was just a few days away.

Chen Guilang was exhausted every day, running back and forth between various departments for lectures and also going to the Science Park to communicate with Guo Feng.

Madman Guo was practically living in the office, developing the campus network day in and day out. Forget attending classes, he didn't even go back to his dorm anymore…

At this moment, Chen Guilang was the only one in dorm room 404.

Senior Min, a sophomore, had dragged Jiang Junlai to the study hall.

The former had signed up for 18 courses, the latter for 20. As long as they didn't have classes at night, they would head to the study hall to review what they learned during the day and read the books required by their professors.

Tired and bored, Chen Guilang called Li Hang from the Yuanhuo Club: "Senior Li Hang, how's the art for *Sanguosha* coming along?"

Li Hang said proudly, "Cao Cao and Liu Bei are done. I'm working on Sun Quan now."

Half a month, and you're telling me you've only finished Cao Cao and Liu Bei?

Fine, don't get angry. The guy has to attend classes too.

Chen Guilang said in a consultative tone, "Senior Li Hang, I'm in a hurry to get the cards printed. How about you find a few more people in the Yuanhuo Club? You can all collaborate to speed things up. I can double your pay."

"Alright… I guess," Li Hang said, a little dejected.

This was his first paid art commission, and he was approaching it with the mindset of an artist, striving for perfection in every detail.

He had only finished two pieces, and now the client was already rushing him.

After hanging up, Chen Guilang called Hu Weishi from *Mengya*.

"Weishi-jie, I've sent the first thirty thousand words of *Those Happenings of the Ming Dynasty* to your email."

"I read it this afternoon. The creative angle is very novel, writing history with a witty and humorous tone. But the readers of *Mengya* are mostly middle school students. Will they like it?"

"They're exactly the target audience for this book, I think it will work. Of course, if Weishi-jie isn't satisfied, I'll give up on serializing it in *Mengya*."

"How about this, I'll try running it for two issues. If the reception is good, we'll continue. If not, we'll cut it. What do you think?"

"That works. After it's serialized in *Mengya*, how soon can I post the serialized content on the forum?"

"After a month and a half."

"Okay. Please try to publish as much as possible in each issue."

"We'll see how the layout goes."

*Mengya*'s serialized novels were about 20,000 words per issue, give or take 5,000, depending on the layout.

The content of one issue in *Mengya* was enough for Chen Guilang to split into ten chapters for the forum.

He should probably get a computer this weekend. With Guo Feng's computer moved to the office, not having one in the dorm was really inconvenient.

Estimating the time, Chen Guilang headed out for the dinner gathering.

A few classmates were already waiting at the school gate. Chen Guilang recognized all of them and remembered their names, but he couldn't quite match all the faces to the names.

The handsome, clean-featured Zhao Beibei was also there.

Chen Guilang had a deep impression of this guy, who had a rather feminine face for a boy.

Senior Long Xiang arrived two minutes before the agreed time, jogging over and panting. As soon as he arrived, he shouted, "Splurge, splurge, let's eat and drink our fill tonight!"

He led everyone to find a restaurant outside the South Gate, not a barbecue place.

There were 12 people in total. One table wasn't big enough, so they pushed two square tables together.

Before the food even arrived, Long Xiang stood up and raised his glass: "Today is our group's first get-together. Let's start with a toast. For those who don't drink, tea or juice is fine."

"Cheers!"

They clinked glasses and sat back down.

Long Xiang said, "I'm guessing not everyone knows each other yet. Let's all get reacquainted tonight and also share our experiences and thoughts from the past two weeks. Of course, you don't have to talk about anything you'd rather not."

"I'll go first."

"You can just speak from your seat. It's a gathering of friends, let's not make it feel like a formal report."

A short, thin girl with glasses said, "My name is Jiang Yuxiu, from the Wu-Yue region. I signed up for 16 courses. Every professor is excellent, and I can't bear to miss a single class. I also joined the May Fourth Literary Society, the Shanying Club, and the Drama Club, and I've participated in activities for all three. Every day for me has been incredibly fulfilling. My feeling is that Peking University has provided us with countless outstanding resources, and we can't waste our youth…"

Sixteen courses plus three clubs. This girl was quite the go-getter.

One by one, they finished speaking. Chen Guilang discovered that everyone was quite the go-getter.

And as for our hero, Chen, he was the one who had signed up for the fewest classes!

"Chen Guilang, it's your turn," Long Xiang reminded him with a smile.

Chen Guilang said, "I chose 14 courses and joined the Yuanhuo Anime Club. My thoughts are similar to everyone else's. It's been very fulfilling, or to be precise, downright exhausting."

Zhao Beibei, who lived on the same floor as Chen Guilang, immediately spilled the beans: "You've also started two companies. Everyone in the Yuanpei Program on the fourth floor of Building 36 is talking about it."

"Started companies?"

The counselor, Long Xiang, and the other group members all looked at him in surprise.

Chen Guilang smiled, "I've just signed two occupancy agreements with the Beida Science Park. The business licenses haven't even been processed yet. And with the National Day holiday coming up, which doesn't count as business days, it'll probably be a long wait."

Long Xiang remarked with emotion, "That's still incredible, starting companies right after enrolling."

"Do you want us to help out?" a boy named Tang Yong asked.

Chen Guilang said, "We're all just freshmen. I'm afraid I'd interfere with everyone's studies. If you're willing to help, I'd welcome you with open arms. But the companies are just starting out, so I can't afford to pay salaries, and I don't need too many people for now."

A girl named Song Lei said, "Just let us know if you need help. As long as we have time, we don't need any pay. We can just treat it as gaining work experience."

"Then I thank all my brothers and sisters," Chen Guilang said, raising his glass.

What followed was casual conversation over dinner, as they shared stories about people and things they'd encountered recently.

All the courses for the Yuanpei Program used the professors and classrooms of other departments. Most of the faculty and students in those departments were reasonably nice to them, and some were even especially enthusiastic out of curiosity. But there were also a few who were subtly exclusionary, especially in smaller classes.

One girl was on the verge of tears as she spoke, saying she planned to switch to a different course.

Long Xiang said he would help communicate with her academic advisor, then quickly changed the subject to keep the atmosphere of the gathering lively.

"Chen Guilang, why didn't you join the May Fourth Society? Our president knows I'm in the Yuanpei Program and specifically mentioned you, asking me to persuade you to join," Jiang Yuxiu asked.

Chen Guilang said, "Your president knows me?"

Jiang Yuxiu said, "There are a lot of poets in the May Fourth Society, and quite a few who write classical-style poetry. Many members of the May Fourth Society know about your poem, *Ballad of Yinghai*."

Peking University's May Fourth Literary Society had a long history, with poetry as its core. Hai Zi had been a member of the society.

One could even say that the Misty Poets movement was driven by the May Fourth Society.

But the golden age of poetry had long passed. Although the society's membership was growing, its influence was a shadow of its former self.

Chen Guilang said, "I'm starting companies, I just don't have the time."

"That's such a pity, your classical poetry is so good," Jiang Yuxiu hadn't given up. "Our president said that you can join anytime you want. He also hopes you can participate in the Weiming Poetry Convention next spring."

"I'll join when I have the time," Chen Guilang did not refuse outright.
